title: Make drain work items in athena plan's order and log passed-over items
summary: Find why drain's order differs from athena plan (a priority record is ignored by drain's entry building, and ready item 20261029-233021-e5sg was skipped silently), so drain follows the same Plan order and logs one line (item, reason) per passed-over planned item. Goal: the owner running drain gets the order plan prints. Follow-up to jobs 20261029-142858-5c0p, 20261029-233021-e5sg and 20261029-142902-5x4h, which are named as evidence only.

defaults_applied.how: New tests plus cargo test and clippy -D warnings pass.
Fix the shared cause of drain/plan divergence, not the one item.
Criteria run the drain entry point and check the order and log lines.
One focused change in drain.rs, plan.rs and CHANGELOG.md.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (drain at ~1892, drain_concurrent ~1903, drain_with ~1921; the planner path at ~1451-1483 builds entries via Steps::plan_entry and Plan::build_with; RealSteps::entry_of at ~2360 applies a priority record (record.priority()) only inside the `if let Some(work) = proposal` branch, otherwise it relies on reading::plan_entry), crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs (Plan::build_with ~521, effective_priorities ~454, priority_violations ~479, position ~632) and crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (set_priority ~777). The suspected cause is that drain builds entries differently from athena plan (priority record not applied for non-proposal jobs, and the per-item path at ~1946 may take the first queued item instead of the plan's first); the producer must confirm by reproducing before fixing. No record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not affected.

Job 20261029-142858-5c0p: its candidate changed nothing and its failure was a kill switch, so nothing there is kept or fixed; it is the evidence of the ignored low priority record only. Its listed files (run/mod.rs, disk.rs, producer.rs, state.rs, design docs, decisions) are out of scope and are not re-done here.

Job 20261029-233021-e5sg: rejected; its candidate files CHANGELOG.md, crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, crates/athena-core/src/store.rs and crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs are not touched by this job and its findings are not addressed here. It is only the planned-first item the drain skipped, and it stays queued for its own retry. CHANGELOG.md is edited here only to add the new entry.

Job 20261029-142902-5x4h: landed; its candidate files crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs and CHANGELOG.md are kept as landed. Its minor findings (read-ahead off in production, wiring note, recheck default, pick_ahead budget nit) are left alone, except where the read-ahead picking could be the cause of skipping the planned-first item; that is fixed only if it is the root cause.

Drain's order must come from the same Plan (same entries, same priority rules, same history) as athena plan, so there is one ordering source. A planned item that is not worked (held, refused, not ready, a clash with a running batch, over budget) gets one log line naming the item id and the reason.

plan.rs changes only if the root cause or a shared helper (for example a function both plan and drain call to build the ordered list) needs it; reading.rs is listed with a low probability for the same reason.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test through the drain entry point (drain or drain_concurrent in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs) with a priority record that lowers an urgent-text request to low shows the drain works that request after a higher-priority item; run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain` and the test passes, and fails on the base code.

A new test shows the order in which the drain works items equals the order athena plan prints (Plan::build_with over the same entries and history) for the same queue, including a ready group-1 item that was previously skipped; run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`.
A new test shows an item the drain passes over gets exactly one log line that names the item id and the reason; run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain` and check the captured log.

The diff in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (and plan.rs if changed) removes the root cause of the divergence: the drain's entry building and ordering share the same code as athena plan, not a second copy of the rule. The summary states the cause found.
The existing drain tests with max_in_flight = 1 pass unchanged; run `cargo test`.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry under Fixed describing that the drain now follows athena plan's order and logs passed-over items with a reason.

out_of_scope: Retrying or fixing jobs 20261029-142858-5c0p, 20261029-233021-e5sg (status.rs, store.rs, athena-git changes) or 20261029-142902-5x4h's findings; their candidates are not touched
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github/workflows or records/
Changing the priority rules themselves (urgent/high/normal/low semantics) beyond making drain and plan agree
departures: Hard ordering change in a large drain.rs with a not-yet-confirmed root cause; costs and pass odds are somewhat worse than the reference.
urgent_reason: It stops the drain dispatching low-priority or wrong items ahead of urgent ones, which wastes runs and builds on work the owner did not want next.
hard_reason: It changes the run pipeline's drain ordering, which decides which queued work is dispatched and when, so a mistake is costly and hard to see.
